rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L02.html Problem M3 solution line 401 (lower bound on x_m)
rows.evidence: New since 4de5291; re-derived. h(x) = P(Z > x) - x phi(x)/(1 + x^2); d/dx[x/(1+x^2)] = (1 - x^2)/(1+x^2)^2 and phi' = -x phi give h'(x) = -phi(x)[(1+x^2)^2 + 1 - 2x^2 - x^4]/(1+x^2)^2 = -2 phi(x)/(1+x^2)^2 < 0, as printed; a numerical derivative matches the formula to 7 digits at x = 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 4. h -> 0 as x -> infinity, so h > 0 for x > 0. At x_m = Phi^-1(1 - alpha/m) > 0: alpha/m > x_m phi(x_m)/(1 + x_m^2); taking logs gives x_m^2 > 2 ln(m/alpha) - 2 ln(sqrt(2 pi)(x_m + 1/x_m)), exactly as printed. Checked numerically at m = 10, 100, 1e3, 1e4, 1e6, 1e9 (6.635 > 6.586, 10.828 > 10.805, 15.137 > 15.124, ...). With Prop 4.1, x_m <= sqrt(2 ln(m/(2 alpha))) makes the log term O(ln ln m), so x_m/sqrt(2 ln m) -> 1 (ratio 1.200, 1.084, 1.047, 1.029, 1.013, 1.0045). The last step is terse, but it follows at once from the cited bound.

The row reads 'Bonferroni critical values grow no faster than sqrt(2 ln(m/(2 alpha))), so power falls as the family grows'. The 'so' does not follow: an upper bound on the critical value cannot imply that power falls. Power falls because Phi^-1(1 - alpha/m) increases with m, and power Phi(mu - c) decreases in c. Neither fact is stated in Proposition 4.1 or proved in section 4; Example 4.2 shows it numerically. The row is unchanged since 4de5291, but round 1 checked only its first clause (round-1 row L02-math-prop41-title), and a T-graded key result must state a valid inference.
